requirement:
# REQ-2234: The analyzer does not work if SuppressSourceGeneration = true

Source: https://github.com/MessagePack-CSharp/MessagePack-CSharp/issues/2234

#### Bug description

The analyzer does not work if SuppressSourceGeneration = true. This has happened since version 3.1.1. It still worked in 3.1.0.

story.summary: The change hardens `TypeCollector` so collecting members no longer throws on bad key layouts. After reporting a mixed int/string key diagnostic it now skips the member (lines 1008 and 1148). It also stops calling `Dictionary.Add` for a key that is already present (1023-1026, 1039-1042, 1163-1166, 1179-1182). It adds analyzer tests and run-time round-trip tests for `[MessagePackObject(SuppressSourceGeneration = true)]` types, plus a README section that lists which diagnostics apply to suppressed types.
story.why: REQ-2234 says analyzer diagnostics stop appearing for types marked `SuppressSourceGeneration = true` (a regression since 3.1.1). The implied root cause is that the collector threw an exception on these code paths (duplicate keys, or `intKey!.Value` on a null key after a mixed-key diagnostic), which killed the analyzer. The diff never shows how `SuppressSourceGeneration` itself is handled, so the link between this fix and the reported regression is inferred, not shown.
touches_beyond_requirement: README.md gains a new 'Opting out of source generation' section that documents analyzer behavior, including MsgPack012 and MsgPack011/016/017 claims that no test in the diff exercises (MsgPack012), or that the diff only checks as absent (011/016/017).

The `TypeCollector` changes also apply to normal (non-suppressed) source-generated types. A member with a duplicate key or mismatched key kind is now silently dropped from the collected model instead of throwing.
story.confidence_overview: Medium that the collector no longer crashes on duplicate or mixed keys. The guards are simple and the new tests target those cases. Low-to-medium that this is the actual fix for REQ-2234. No changed line references `SuppressSourceGeneration`, and nothing shows these tests failed before the change. The execution test `NoFormatterIsGeneratedForSuppressedType` asserts nothing about formatter absence.

claims.text: The analyzer tests check that MsgPack004, MsgPack015, MsgPack003 and MsgPack005 are reported for `SuppressSourceGeneration = true` types. This is the user-visible symptom in the requirement. Nothing in the diff shows these tests failed before the change, so whether they reproduce the regression is unverified.

findings.description: Claim C3 disputed: All production changes in the diff are shown in full (TypeCollector.cs +18/-4), contradicting 'Nothing in the diff shows these tests failed before the change' in both directions: (1) for the three MsgPack005 tests (SuppressSourceGenerationAnalyzerTests.cs lines 80-144), TypeCollector.cs directly shows they did fail before the change because unconditional intMembers.Add/stringMembers.Add (lines 1023 and 1039) threw ArgumentException on duplicate keys and missing continue (line 1008) fell through to intKey!.Value (line 1019) throwing InvalidOperationException on mixed keys, causing AD0001 analyzer failure; (2) for the MsgPack004, MsgPack015, and MsgPack003 tests (lines 20-78), each input has at most one keyed member and never hits any branch modified in TypeCollector.cs, proving this change does not alter their behavior and only addresses REQ-2234 when duplicate or mixed keys crash TypeCollector.

None of the changed lines mention `SuppressSourceGeneration`. The fix assumes the 3.1.1 regression was an exception thrown during member collection, but the diff does not show this. If suppressed types are skipped or short-circuited somewhere else (for example, an early return before member analysis), the reported bug would remain. The new analyzer tests would show that only if they were confirmed to fail on the old code.

`continue` skips every later per-member step for the mixed-key member. That includes the `[MessagePackFormatter]` lookup and member-type validation (MsgPack003) further down. As a result, diagnostics on that member may now be hidden until the key issue is fixed.

A `stringMembers.ContainsKey(stringKey!)` check already exists just above (lines 1030/1170), so the new guard may be redundant, or that branch may not `continue`. With the new guard, a duplicate member is silently dropped from the collected model for generated types. That is acceptable only if the duplicate diagnostic is always an error that blocks the build.

`NoFormatterIsGeneratedForSuppressedType` only asserts that `GeneratedMessagePackResolver.Instance` is not null. It does not check that no formatter was generated for `SuppressedSourceGenerationType`, so the test name overstates what is checked.
The README says MsgPack012 (accessibility) is reported for suppressed types, but no test in the diff covers that case.

NoFormatterIsGeneratedForSuppressedType only asserts Assert.NotNull(GeneratedMessagePackResolver.Instance) and never asserts Assert.Null(GeneratedMessagePackResolver.Instance.GetFormatter<SuppressedSourceGenerationType>()). If SuppressSourceGeneration = true regresses and emits a formatter, both tests in SuppressedSourceGenerationTests.cs will still pass.

The field-loop fixes in TypeCollector.cs (mixed keys at line 1148, duplicate int keys at lines 1163-1166, and duplicate string keys at lines 1179-1182) have no test coverage in SuppressSourceGenerationAnalyzerTests.cs, where all duplicate-key and mixed-key test cases (lines 81-166) only declare properties.

README.md claims MsgPack012 is still reported for SuppressSourceGeneration = true types, but SuppressSourceGenerationAnalyzerTests.cs has no test verifying MsgPack012 is emitted when source generation is suppressed.
